claims.text: Deep neural networks in natural language processing are vulnerable to adversarial examples.
Adversarial perturbation methods designed for images cannot be directly applied to text because textual data is discrete.
Small textual perturbations are easily perceptible to humans compared to small image perturbations.
Character or word level perturbations can drastically alter sentence semantics.
Adversarial training is more effective than defensive distillation against adversarial attacks on models handling discrete data.

evidence.description: Previous efforts have shown that DNNs were vulnerable to strategically modified samples, named adversarial examples, which fool DNNs to give false predictions.
Existing perturbation methods for images cannot be directly applied to texts as text data is discrete in nature.
For adversarial attack on texts, small perturbations are easily perceptible, generating invalid words or syntactically incorrect sentences.
Replacement of characters or words would alter the semantics of the sentence drastically, e.g., deleting a negation word changes sentence sentiment.
Evaluations in reviewed literature showed that adversarial training is more effective than distillation for models operating on discrete data.

methodologies.name: Literature Survey and Taxonomy Construction
methodologies.description: Systematic collection, selection, and categorization of adversarial attack and defense literature in natural language processing across threat models, attack granularity, and applications.

limitations.text: Detailed evaluation metrics for specific NLP tasks are declared out of scope and omitted from detailed coverage in this survey.
Existing textual adversarial attack methods exhibit poor generalization and significant performance drops when transferred across different target architectures or datasets.
Many black-box textual adversarial generation techniques rely on manual construction rather than automated end-to-end execution.

future_work.text: Develop practical textual attack methods that make perturbations unperceivable while strictly preserving correct grammar and sentence semantics.
Investigate adversarial attacks targeting deep generative textual models such as Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and Variational Auto-Encoders (VAEs).
Improve cross-model and cross-dataset transferability and generalization capabilities of textual adversarial attacks.
